    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    A familiar Iranian hacking group has found a newly introduced way to cause chaos

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history: cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food.
    • According to recent reports, hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe.
    • Industry observers note that the unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    One night in October, hackers staged one of the most unusual cyber attacks in history: cranking up the temperature in refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets across France and destroying millions of euros of food.

    According to recent reports, hackers have targeted commercial fridges and freezers before, but never at this scale and never in the heart of Europe. The brazen attack left cyber professionals unsure as to who might have executed such a madcap operation. But French intelligence agencies found traces of Farsi and other clues in the digital trail pointing to an elite hacking unit of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

    Industry observers note that the unit allegedly behind the hack, Shahid Kaveh, was already well known to Western intelligence agencies. Named after Mahmoud Kaveh, an Iranian commander who died during the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, it is one of several hacking units overseen by the Revolutionary Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command.

    According to recent reports, the group, which often goes by the online persona CyberAv3ngers, has a history of targeting critical infrastructure. In 2023 and 2024, it hacked Israeli-made industrial control devices inside water, manufacturing, and transportation systems across several US states. Operational disruption was minimal, but the attackers left a message each time: “Every equipment ‘made in Israel’ is CyberAv3ngers legal target.”.

    Sources indicate that state-backed Iranian hackers have rarely targeted Europe in this way, however. October’s hacks, experts say, mark an escalation in the Islamic republic’s cyber warfare strategy and a latest willingness to hit European infrastructure.

    “Iran has very clearly messaged that the global economy will be disrupted as a consequence of it being shut out from the world,” stated Ellie Geranmayeh of the European Council on Foreign Relations.

    Industry observers note that while France and other European countries have largely stayed out of the US and Israel’s campaign against Iran, which started in February, the Islamic republic increasingly views all Nato countries as legitimate targets, she continued. “This is about sowing panic in Europe and increasing that global pain threshold.”.

    Similar attacks were staged this month against supermarkets in 10 other countries across Europe, though no group has yet been blamed.

    Industry observers note that iran has denied any role in the freezer hacks, but France is seeking international arrest warrants for three Iranians allegedly involved: Hamid Reza Lashgarian, believed by US intelligence to be head of the Guards’ Cyber Electronic Command, and two Shahid Kaveh leaders, 37-year-old Mahdi Lashgarian and 35-year-old Reza Salarvand. Both Lashgarians were placed under US sanctions in 2024.

    Often staffed with young engineers and software developers, the Revolutionary Guards’ cyber units have developed formidable skills in espionage and cyber warfare.

    Industry observers note that “Iran is a country of engineers, and people continue to underestimate its capabilities,” mentioned Sanam Vakil, Middle East director at Chatham House think-tank. “It has a long history of successful cyber operations,” she added, noting that Iran had learnt through its own experience of cyber attacks, most notably the Stuxnet assault on its nuclear program by the US and Israel in 2009.

    In a recent development, french intelligence agencies have said the group used a Chinese-made scanning tool to scour the public Internet for connected refrigeration units. Infrastructure linked to the group also conducted reconnaissance using Modbus, a digital language widely used to control industrial machinery—a technique Shahid Kaveh has employed since at least April, according to the authorities.

    The modus operandi described by the French authorities was consistent with the Iranian attacks in the US in 2023 and 2024, said Cynthia Kaiser, former deputy cyber director at the FBI. Near-identical hacks to those have taken place this year, though CyberAv3ngers did not claim responsibility, and US authorities stopped short of explicitly blaming Iran.

    Industry observers note that kaiser stated it was also possible that a third state could have contracted Shahid Kaveh to conduct the European attacks. “Even if Iranians were behind the keyboard, these attacks really appear more consistent with Russian-type targeting,” she said. “It wouldn’t surprise me if we eventually uncovered collaboration behind the scenes.”.

    Russia, like Iran, has sophisticated cyber capabilities and has shown increasing willingness to use them against Europe.

    Sources indicate that vakil at Chatham House acknowledged Russian involvement remained a possibility, noting that the strength of the relationship between the two countries was often under-appreciated by Western officials. “Their ties have grown through the context of these wars,” she noted, referring to Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine and Iran’s conflict with the US and Israel. In March, Russian state-sponsored hacking group NoName claimed responsibility for a series of attacks on Israeli targets.

    Whether or not Shahid Kaveh was working on behalf of Moscow or another power, the operation would have to be sanctioned by the senior leadership of the IRGC, according to Gil Messing, chief of staff at Israeli cyber security group Check Point Software.

    Cyber weapons have a limited shelf life, as once a specific software or hardware vulnerability has been exploited, it tends to be almost immediately patched by other potential targets.

    “The decision to make such a thing and burn out this capability is something that would have to be authorized by senior levels,” Messing stated. “This is not a very sophisticated attack, but it sends a very strong message.”.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Dozens of people were killed in August after a rubbish landfill collapsed in Conakry.
    • Guinea has ordered residents to do a mass clean-up of the capital, Conakry, months after a rubbish landfill collapsed, killing dozens of people.
    • Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday revealed a deadline of 31 December to clear rubbish in the city and its suburbs, which has seen an increase in illegal dumping in recent months.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Dozens of people were killed in August after a rubbish landfill collapsed in Conakry.

    Guinea has ordered residents to do a mass clean-up of the capital, Conakry, months after a rubbish landfill collapsed, killing dozens of people.

    Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah on Wednesday revealed a deadline of 31 December to clear rubbish in the city and its suburbs, which has seen an increase in illegal dumping in recent months.

    In August heavy rains caused a landslide at the capital's main waste dump, with the rubbish collapsing onto homes killing 31 people and injuring others.

    The site in the city's Dar es Salaam area was subsequently closed permanently, which has led to piles of rubbish accumulating outside homes and on the streets.

    At a public forum on sanitation, Sanitation Minister Aboubacar Camara said Conakry was generating about 3,000 tonnes of waste every day.

    He said much of the garbage was ending up in the streets because of weaknesses in the collection system.

    The prime minister called on local authorities to become more involved in organising waste collection, saying this could become a way to create jobs.

    "The state will do its part, but the municipalities must also organise themselves to ensure waste collection and provide jobs for young people," the prime minister remarked.

    "Conakry must be completely clean by the end of December," he added, relaying a directive from the country's president, Mamady Doumbouya.

    He cited measures the government was taking to improve waste collection and recycling, including a national sanitation fund that would guarantee financing for the sector.

    Camara mentioned talks had been finalised with a waste collection operator, with a initiative for equipment to move waste from transit and sorting centres to a new disposal site in BaretodÃ©, outside the capital.

    The August tragedy at the Dar es Salaam landfill was not the first - 10 people were killed at the same site in 2017.

    The government had ordered people living close to the site to move, but many residents chose to stay.

    According to the prime minister, the government now prepares to transform the closed waste site into an urban park.

For the first time in years, he can handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, or a loved one's hand.

    Davidson is the ninth person to have this experimental device implanted, but he's the first to take it home and use it independently. Researchers hope his experiences will reveal how useful the technology really is in day-to-day life, and how it might affect his brain and nervous system.

    Upcoming UK-EU treaty has 10-year termination clause

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The government and the EU have published the texts of two treaties agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset.
    • The treaties were published on Thursday afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.
    • The deal covering food exports has a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement, they would have to pay "reasonable and proportionate costs" to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the newly introduced deal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The government and the EU have published the texts of two treaties agreed last week as part of a post-Brexit reset.

    The treaties were published on Thursday afternoon, alongside legislation designed to enact the bulk of the deal.

    The deal covering food exports has a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party ended the agreement, they would have to pay "reasonable and proportionate costs" to rebuild border checks infrastructure, which will be significantly scaled back as part of the newly introduced deal.

    Opposition leader Kemi Badenoch has stated she would scrap the deal while Reform UK's Nigel Farage has suggested he would refuse to pay.

    The Brexit reset deal has already sparked debate about its benefits, its costs, and a wider discussion on the future of the UK-EU relationship.

    The deal covers British food exports, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme.

    Two of the three legal texts were released on Thursday, covering the food trade and emissions trading scheme deals, alongside the government's cost-cutting bill to enact the deal.

    A new assessment of the impact of the deal on different sectors and regions of the country was also released.

    EU offers UK fresh deal on 'Made in Europe' scheme.

    Badenoch challenges Burnham over university fees for EU students.

    Farage helps launch new campaign against the UK rejoining the EU.

    According to recent reports, under the deal, food exporters will be significant beneficiaries from the scrapping of considerable red tape and checks, and dismantling of border facilities. An internal analysis forecasts a 16% boost the export of major agricultural commodities.

    The industry and government hope the reduction in costs for food producers and sellers will be passed on to customers, but there may be no clear visible impact at the checkout.

    Privately, industry insiders told the BBC earlier this week that there are too many moving parts in the world economy, in particular the energy price shock resulting from war in the Middle East.

    Regarding the fine detail in the text of one of the treaties relating to the 10-year termination clause, European affairs minister Hamish Falconer remarked: "The Cutting Costs Bill allows us to implement two major trade agreements.".

    "It allows us to eliminate paperwork for our food and drink traders, protect billions of pounds worth of British exports from carbon taxes, and make doing business with our largest trading partner cheaper and easier.".

    A plan to link British and European emissions trading schemes will see more coverage across the UK's aviation and maritime industries.

    According to recent reports, the treaty text also contains finer detail of how the UK will observe, shape but not vote on relevant EU rules. The UK will be invited to attend European Commission meetings and expert groups as an observer, as well as taking part in emergency food security planning.

    However, the UK will not be given voting rights.

    Plans to use secondary legislation, including granting direct so-called "Henry VIII powers" to ministers to align UK and EU laws, are detailed in the legislation.

    Such powers will enable ministers to make changes to bills with less Parliamentary scrutiny.

    Outlining the agreement with the EU to MPs earlier this week, the prime minister mentioned newly introduced agreements with the EU are "pragmatic" and "not a prelude to anything".

    Andy Burnham also noted it would be "unthinkable" for the UK to rejoin the bloc without a referendum.

    Several former prime ministers have urged him not to reopen the Brexit debate. Burnham noted they are "stuck in the past" and later claimed there would be "no banging on about Europe" from Labour.

    Badenoch noted Burnham has "oversold" the deal and was "trying to take Britain back to 2015".

    I was more excited for Nothing’s latest device when I thought it was an AI vape pen.

    Ahead of December 8 and too many coordinated leaks to count, Nothing has officially declared its first "AI-native" device. Somewhat anticlimactically, the Ear (note) is a pair of earbuds with built-in AI notetaking. As the company told Bloomberg, the earbuds can transcribe and summarize in-person conversations, calls, online meetings and voice memos, in addition to offering traditional audio playback with Hi-Res audio support.

    "Ear (note) is part of Nothing's vision to build the hardware context layer of AI, bringing intelligence closer to the moments, conversations and experiences that shape our everyday lives," the firm wrote in a press release it shared with Engadget.

    No information on pricing or specs just yet, but Nothing promised to share more details soon. The company describes the Ear (note) as a "new approach to personal productivity," but Nothing is not the first to announce earbuds with built-in AI transcription. This past August, Plaud debuted its own pair of AI-forward earbuds in the form of the Plaud One. That said, if you're a fan of Nothing's design, you'll be sure to appreciate the Sony Walkman-like design the company has gone for, especially when it comes to the new Record and Talk buttons along the bottom of the aluminum case.

    The Ear (note) will launch on December 8.

    10 Best Office Chairs of 2026—We Tested 70 to Pick Them

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that there Are Three things you don’t skimp on if you want a happy life: a good mattress, a good pair of shoes, and the best office chair you can find.
    • The best desk chair is almost always an adjustable chair—one that can be tailored to your body’s unique shape and that offers enough lumbar support to avoid back problems even after long hours at the grind.
