    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    These tools will make turkey day just a little easier.

    We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

    It has been revealed that thanksgiving is supposed to be a time for rest, relaxation and appreciating all the good things that have happened to you over the past year. However, there's no denying that it's also a ton of work for whoever is in charge of preparing your Thanksgiving meal. Not only do you have to consider the cooking itself, there's all the other things that come with making a holiday feast like choosing the right recipes, gathering all the ingredients and scheduling which dishes need to be cooked at what time so everything is ready together. And all that doesn't even include managing anyone who feels like helping, which can turn into its own logistical problem.

    So to help smooth out the chaos that is holiday cooking, we've put together a collection of essential cooking gadgets that can save you time and take some of the stress out of preparing your Thanksgiving bounty.

    Recent findings suggest that most people probably wouldn't consider a knife to be very techy, and for most blades that sentiment rings true. But on days like Thanksgiving where you're going to be doing a ton of chopping, cutting, slicing and more, it can't hurt to have a little extra help. And then there's the turkey, because it isn't going to carve itself. Furthermore, if you want your bird to look anything like it does in cooking videos with those neat, super clean slices, you're going to need a sharp tool to get there.

    It has been revealed that for cooking nerds who like to geek out about the science of sharpness, one of my favorite knives on the market right now is the Seattle Ultrasonics C-200. In addition to just being a really nice knife featuring a three-layer san mai blade made out of Japanese AUS-10 steel, inside its handle there's a motor that vibrates the knife 30,000 times per second. While the oscillations are so small that you can't actually feel it shaking, those vibrations increased the knife's effective sharpness by up to 50 percent. It excels at delicate foods like tomatoes that often like to stick to the side of your blade, but also denser things like potatoes and meat, which obviously includes turkey. The C-200 even comes with an IP65 rating for dust and water resistance, so there's no worry about ruining its electronics with an errant splash. And if you opt for the wireless charging tile, you'll never have to worry about keeping its battery topped up. Granted, starting at $399, it certainly isn't cheap, but that price is very much in the same range as other premium chef knives from substantial name companies like Shun, Wusthoff and others.

    Alternatively, if you want a dedicated gadget for helping you carve a turkey, you can always turn to more traditional electric knives like those from Cusinart, NutriChef, Hamilton Beach and more. Admittedly, these types of knives aren't nearly as pretty as blades like the C200 and the need to plug them in makes them harder to use on an everyday basis. But if you want a relatively easy and affordable way to make serving your Thanksgiving turkey go a bit more smoothly, a classic electric knife is definitely worth a look.

    It has been revealed that even if you prefer side dishes like mashed potatoes, stuffing or a green bean casserole, there's no denying that the turkey is the star of Thanksgiving dinner. And if you want it to come out just right, you need a decent thermometer. Not having one is basically gambling that you get lucky with your timing and the bird turns out well. That said, there are a range of options, from simple digital sticks like the affordable ThermoPop 2 to fancy probe thermometers like the second-gen model from Combustion Inc.

    Industry observers note that basic options require a bit more work as you can't leave them in the bird while it's in the oven, whereas more expensive versions have wireless support that allows you to leave them inside the turkey as it cooks. Some options like those from Combustion Inc. even account for carry-over cooking, which is when the temperature of the food continues to rise even after you take it out of the oven. You just need to decide how much you want to spend and what kind of features you really want. One of my more affordable favorites is the Sense from Chef IQ, which offers a great balance between price and performance. Just don't be a fool and try to rely strictly on the little pop-out thermometers that sometimes come with the bird, as those aren't known for their accuracy or precision.

    Industry observers note that A massive matter during Thanksgiving is not having enough room in your oven for everything that needs to be baked or roasted. One easy solution to this is turning to an air fryer, which works almost exactly like the convection function on an oven, but in a smaller volume that's faster to heat and sometimes offers better air circulation. Another really nice thing about air fryers is that they can be quite affordable, with name brand models like the Instant Pot Vortex or the Ninja Air Fryer Pro, both of which are at the moment going for as little as $80.

    It has been revealed that upgrading to more expensive fryers like the Philips 3000 can give you more capacity, while even pricier options like the Wonder Oven Pro from Our Place have as many as eight different functions for things like baking, roasting, dehydrating, proofing and more. And perhaps the best thing is that when the holidays are over, you can easily move these into your pantry, closet or garage and reclaim some of your precious kitchen counter space.

    It has been revealed that A good digital scale falls in the same general camp as a decent thermometer and there isn't an experienced baker that would be caught dead without one. They're super easy to use and in my opinion, they are a staple of any well-equipped kitchen. You can just plop a mixing bowl on top, zero out the scale and then add ingredients in as needed while you get precise measurements, which can be especially critical for baked goods and confections. OXO makes a very nice and rather affordable digital scale that starts at around $65, but you can find cheaper options from well-known brands like KitchenAid for barely more than $20.

    Industry observers note that A lot of people think blenders are big, bulky contraptions that make a ton of noise and take up too much room in your kitchen. And while the most powerful ones often are, they don't need to be, as there are affordable options that aren't much bigger than a teapot like these ones from Magic Bullet and Ninja. Regardless, they are great for making a post-dinner milkshake or a lovely fall-inspired soup (butternut squash anyone?).

    According to recent reports, alternatively, you can opt for an immersion blender (aka a hand blender), which can do much of the same functions as a big countertop model, but gives you even greater control and the ability to blend things directly on the stovetop using the pots you already own. This can make them better choices for whipping up sauces like hollandaise (which is delicious when poured over roasted asparagus), mayonnaise or even a classic cranberry sauce to go with your turkey. I prefer cordless options like those from KitchenAid as they have more than enough battery life to complete multiple dishes and the lack of a wire makes them super easy to use. But if your budget is tight, traditional cabled options are totally fine too and often a more affordable choice.

    In a recent development, even for people like me who prefer to chop things by hand, a food processor can be an incredible time saver during the holidays. Not only do they make quick minces of veggies, they can also be used to grate cheese, shred things like potatoes (for an easy Thanksgiving hash), or whip up dips like salsa. Some options like the Cusinart Mini Food processor are stupendously cheap at under $30, while pricer models like the Ninja Professional Plus Food Processor come with a bunch of attachments to handle all sorts of dishes.

    Recent findings suggest that cooking food in a water bath might seem like an unnecessarily complex thing to do for the holidays, but it can actually save you time and effort. A good sous vide machine like those from Anova or Breville allow you to set an exact temperature and hold it there almost indefinitely. This allows you to cook things like meat with precision, so there's no worrying about if something is going to come out medium-rare or well-done.

    And even on Thanksgiving where turkey is the main protein, you can still use a sous vide machine to make dishes like superb rosemary mashed potatoes or luscious glazed carrots. Some models even come with Wi-Fi, so you can start and set them remotely using your phone. On top of that, all they need to function is an outlet, so a sous vide machine can be a great option for people with small kitchens or a limited number of burners on their stove.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bayern Munich's disappointing 2-1 Champions League defeat at Lille on Wednesday night – in which Jamal Musiala came on for the last quarter of an hour – was overshadowed by comments the club's captain made afterwards.

    It has been revealed that "It must never happen that something like this is played out at a player's expense. Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than the player, but it's not bigger than the person," Kimmich told reporters in the mixed zone.

    "That's an absolute no-go and not Bayern-like," he added.

    Kimmich was responding to recent comments made by Bayern supervisory board members Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge.

    "If he (Musiala) doesn't return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency – because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable," Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told Sky on Friday.

    Honorary President Uli Hoeness has described the situation as a "dilemma" for the club, while CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen raised the prospect of talks with Musiala's management and family.

    While theGermany player has struggled with a number of injuries over the past couple of seasons, his health came into sharper focus in August, after he collapsed on the pitch in a couple of preseason matches. He subsequently revealed that he had been diagnosed with a neurological condition which causes him to suffer from occasional "absence seizures.".

    Kimmich added that criticism of a players' performances was legitimate, but that concerns about Musiala's situation should have been dealt with behind closed doors.

    "That's something you should sort out internally, around a table, rather than trying to resolve it publicly," he stated.

    According to recent reports, "It's not that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself.".

    Meanwhile, Bayern bosses met with Musiala's agents on Tuesday, and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation that the player could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension.

    Bayern said the two sides agreed that he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after he had signed his contract extension, which makes him one of the club's top earners and is to keep him in Munich until 2030. Discussions between Bayern management and Musiala's representatives are reportedly ongoing.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.
    • Industry observers note that the feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android.
    • Sources indicate that users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    WhatsApp on Wednesday started rolling out a much-sought-after feature: the ability to schedule messages in both individual and group chats.

    Industry observers note that the feature is rolling out globally to all users across iOS and Android. Once it becomes available, you can type a message and long-press the send button to schedule it. You can choose to send a message anywhere between 10 minutes and 14 days later.

    Sources indicate that users will be able to see all their scheduled messages and delete them if needed. It’s not clear if there is a way to edit the schedule of a message.

    Industry observers note that notably, scheduled messages will be sent even if your phone is off or outside network coverage. You can schedule messages containing text, photos, and videos.

    Recent findings suggest that the feature could prove useful for wishing someone a happy birthday on time or chatting with people across time zones. Businesses may also find it easier to schedule texts and updates to their customers, and people who use the app to coordinate work will likely find themselves using scheduled texts to upgrade their teams.

    WhatsApp rivals like Telegram and Signal have had the ability to schedule messages for a while now, so the Meta-owned chat app is late in rolling it out.

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Watch: Fire and smoke billows out of refinery owned by energy organization Bangchak Corporation.
    • Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have said.
    • Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which said the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: Fire and smoke billows out of refinery owned by energy organization Bangchak Corporation.

    Nine people have been injured after an explosion at an oil refinery in Bangkok, authorities have said.

    Three of them are in critical condition, according to news agency AFP, which said the local hospital had revised its earlier assessment of four.

    A fire broke out after the blast at the Phra Khanong facility run by energy giant Bangchak Corporation in the east of Thailand's capital at around 14:45 (07:45 GMT).

    The company said the fire was brought under control and put out within 30 minutes, adding that the cause of the incident was being investigated.

    Black smoke could be seen across Bangkok's skyline after the blast, as local officials told residents to leave the area.

    An alert sent to mobile phones by Bangkok authorities confirmed that the fire was under control, but urged people to avoid the area.

    Eyewitnesses shared video clips on social media of flames and smoke rising above the refinery.

    On a visit to the scene, Thailand's energy minister Akanat Promphan mentioned it appeared the impact of the explosion was limited because the fire started in a distillation tower about 100m (330ft) from where oil was being stored.

    He said the incident was concerning as the refinery was in a residential area and the government was suspending production until it could be confident that operations would resume without any issues.

    Bangchak Corporation stated air quality monitoring in the immediate area around the refinery was within normal ranges.

    According to recent reports, it confirmed that production at the site, which can process up to 120,000 barrels of oil a day had been shut down. The organization has a second refinery in Chonburi province, about 50 miles (80km) from Bangkok, handling a daily capacity of about 180,000 barrels.

    An explosion occurred at the Bangkok refinery in July 2012, sparking a fire but no reported injuries.

    EU-Indonesia trade deal opens newly introduced markets, but challenges remain

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1060 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • As the European Union seeks to deepen its presence in Asia and diversify its trade relationships, Indonesia is emerging as an increasingly important partner.
    • At a signing ceremony in Brussels last week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the bloc's trade agreement with Jakarta as one of its "most ambitious deals" in the region, linking markets of 730 million people.
    • The deal, the culmination of nearly a decade of negotiations, reflects the EU's efforts to diversify its trade partnerships, secure access to critical raw materials and reduce strategic dependencies on China.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As the European Union seeks to deepen its presence in Asia and diversify its trade relationships, Indonesia is emerging as an increasingly important partner.

    At a signing ceremony in Brussels last week, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen described the bloc's trade agreement with Jakarta as one of its "most ambitious deals" in the region, linking markets of 730 million people.

    The deal, the culmination of nearly a decade of negotiations, reflects the EU's efforts to diversify its trade partnerships, secure access to critical raw materials and reduce strategic dependencies on China.

    For Indonesia, it offers opportunities to attract investment, expand exports and strengthen its position in global supply chains.

    The agreement will gradually scrap tariffs on more than 98% of product categories, covering almost the entire value of bilateral trade over 15 years.

    For the EU, gaining better access to critical raw materials, particularly nickel, and diversifying its supply chains are central to its strategic partnership with Indonesia, said Philip Schleifer, an associate professor of political science at the University of Amsterdam.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    "The main strategic interests are opening up a large and growing market for European companies, diversifying and deepening its economic partnerships, reducing strategic dependencies on China, and securing access to critical raw materials," Schleifer told DW.

    Indonesia's mineral resources are particularly key for Europe's green and digital transitions. Nickel, for instance, is a key material for batteries and electric vehicles.

    The agreement also creates opportunities for European investment in strategic sectors, including electric vehicles, electronics and pharmaceuticals.

    But Indonesia has its own industrial ambitions. The government wants to move beyond exporting raw materials by developing domestic processing industries and retaining more value from its natural resources.

    "The challenge for the EU is to reconcile its own interest in securing raw material supply with Indonesia's industrial development objectives," said Eline Blot, a senior policy analyst at the Institute for European Environmental Policy (IEEP).

    Yose Rizal Damuri, an economist at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, stated his institution's study estimates Indonesian exports could increase by around 60% in the coming years.

    "Not only can Indonesia increase exports to Europe, but it can also become more strongly integrated into the global supply chains of European companies," Yose told DW.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Potential beneficiaries include labor-intensive manufacturing sectors such as textiles, garments, footwear and furniture, alongside other Indonesian commodities and manufactured products.

    It has been revealed that the agreement could also encourage European investment and create employment opportunities. However, Yose stressed that access to the European market does not automatically translate into higher exports.

    He identified three priorities for Indonesia: raising awareness of the agreement among domestic businesses, strengthening production capacity and improving the country's business climate.

    Recent findings suggest that "Various trade agreements signed by Indonesia have relatively low utilization rates. The value of exports using these facilities remains limited compared with overall export values," he remarked, emphasizing the need for better information and outreach to producers.

    Syafruddin Karimi, an economist at Andalas University in West Sumatra, also highlighted the opportunity to diversify Indonesia's export markets and reduce dependence on major trading partners such as China, the United States and regional Asian economies.

    However, he warned that Indonesian producers must improve their compliance with European standards.

    "Products must be traceable, including whether their production involves environmental damage or labor practices that undermine human dignity," Karimi said.

    The expansion of trade and investment could also increase environmental pressures, particularly in nickel mining, palm oil production and manufacturing.

    In a recent development, IEEP analyst Blot warned that increased production without stronger environmental safeguards could worsen pollution, ecosystem degradation and industrial emissions. "Nickel mining and processing can contribute to pollution and ecosystem degradation, while palm oil remains closely associated with deforestation," she remarked.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The EU Deforestation Regulation presents another challenge for Indonesian producers, particularly small-scale farmers who may lack the resources, technical capacity and documentation needed to demonstrate compliance.

    Blot acknowledged that these requirements could create disproportionate costs for smaller producers and potentially favor larger companies.

    However, she cautioned against using smallholders' livelihoods as an argument to weaken environmental regulations.

    "Rather than weakening environmental requirements, the priority should be to ensure that smallholders receive adequate financial and technical support to meet them," she remarked.

    Schleifer at the University of Amsterdam also warned that growing global demand for Indonesian natural resources could create environmental and social problems previously associated with commodities such as timber, palm oil and coal.

    While Indonesia has considerable bargaining power because of its mineral wealth, the challenge is ensuring that increased demand translates into domestic industrial development rather than simply expanding resource extraction.

    The agreement includes a dedicated Trade and Sustainable Development chapter covering climate change, biodiversity conservation, sustainable forest management and labor rights. It also provides mechanisms for cooperation and civil society participation.

    However, there is no guarantee these commitments will be implemented. "Experience with other EU trade agreements suggests that there is often a big gap between sustainability commitments on paper and outcomes on the ground," Schleifer stated.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Recent findings suggest that for Indonesia, the challenge also lies in preparing domestic industries to compete. Karimi stressed that the government, both at national and regional levels, must work with businesses to improve production standards, particularly among small and medium-sized enterprises.

    Yose also emphasized the importance of a predictable business environment, warning that frequent policy changes and regulatory uncertainty could discourage investors.

    "Without improvements in the domestic business climate, this will not become a reality. Everything will remain good on paper but will not turn into real momentum for change," he noted.

    Ultimately, the trade agreement offers Indonesia an opportunity to strengthen its position in international trade and attract investment from Europe.

    But whether the agreement delivers broader economic benefits will depend on the country's ability to develop competitive industries, move into higher-value production, and ensure that environmental protection and workers' rights are not overlooked.

    DW's Muhammad Athif Aiman contributed to this article.

    Etsy clarifies AI terms after seller backlash

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (437 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.
    • In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the tech giant’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”.
    • Industry observers note that “Our recent terms upgrade was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After backlash from sellers frustrated by Etsy’s new AI policies, which appeared to allow the company to train AI on user artwork, Etsy has now clarified its stance.

    In a note published on Monday, CEO Kruti Patel Goyal discussed recent tweaks to the tech giant’s terms of service and admitted that her team “should’ve given you more context on what the updates meant for your creative content.”.

    Industry observers note that “Our recent terms upgrade was meant to reflect the evolving technologies we’re using to build better tools and experiences for sellers and the Etsy community,” Goyal wrote this week. “It was not meant to enable us to train AI models for the purpose of creating copycats of your items. We do not and will not do that.”.

    Aaron Meshon, a longtime professional illustrator and Etsy seller, told Ars that even though the tech giant had dialed back its AI language somewhat, the changes were mere “sugar coating.”.

    He noted he still plans on shutting down his 15-year-old Etsy store on December 1.

    “I would say I’m losing 20 percent of my yearly income,” he said. “It’s a few mortgage payments.”.

    He noted that Etsy’s announcement also seems to be rather tone-deaf, given that many retailers make a substantial portion of their annual revenue in the run-up to the end-of-year holiday season.

    “This is the worst two-to-three weeks out of the year to do this, bar none,” he said.

    Recent findings suggest that the fracas began earlier this month, when the company first proposed new contractual language. The updated terms read:.

    As a result, a slew of vendors pulled up stakes, with some saying they had “burned their Etsy shop to the ground” or that they “just killed our Etsy store after 13 years.”.

    Etsy’s change is reminiscent of a recent dust-up involving Meta, where the tech giant had wanted to “require Meta Business account people to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook.” Meta then indefinitely paused that move.

    Last month, Etsy also told sellers that it would “set clearer restrictions on AI use,” despite the fact that AI-generated items remain for sale all over the site.

    According to recent reports, “Today, many active buyers say they can’t tell which items involve AI-generated content,” James Ossman, the company’s vice president of customer operations, wrote on October 22. “It’s become a top-three barrier to shopping more often on Etsy.”.

    For years, Etsy has been notoriously poor at enforcing its own rules, not only regarding AI but also the official prohibitions on selling sex toys, pornography, and even purported witchcraft spells.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.
    • Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales.
    • Industry observers note that there will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rockstar’s behemoth takes up a lot of storage space.

    Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest game of the year by some distance, having racked up $3.79 billion in pre-orders and day-one sales. On PlayStation 5 alone, more than 39 million unique players took control of dual protagonists Jason and Lucia on opening weekend, making it the biggest game debut in the 32-year history of PlayStation.

    Industry observers note that there will be many other folks who want to play the game and haven't had a chance to jump in yet. One thing they should note is that, with a hefty install size, GTA 6 will take up a significant chunk of their PS5 or Xbox Series X/S storage space.

    Recent findings suggest that you might be wondering whether you can install GTA 6 on an external hard drive to avoid having to delete other games and data from your console. You can move GTA 6 to your external storage when you're not playing it. However, to run the game locally, you'll need to have it installed on your system's built-in storage, an SDD you've installed in your PS5 or a compatible NVMe expansion card that's plugged into your Xbox.

    As with many other recent games, GTA 6 needs to take advantage of the fast-loading capabilities of the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. The consoles are unable to load data for these titles quickly enough from an external hard drive over a USB connection. For the same reason, disc-based PS5 and Xbox Series X games are installed onto system storage before you can play them. The PS5 can run PS4 games from external storage, though. Likewise, an Xbox Series X/S can run older Xbox One and Xbox 360 titles directly from an external hard drive.

    X announced fresh creation tools Wednesday, many of them focused on short-form vertical video. The updates are part of the platform’s effort to compete with social networks such as YouTube and Instagram as the format continues to grow in popularity.

    It has been revealed that the tools are designed to help creators make professional-quality vertical videos, share original content more easily, and earn more. They also give creators more ways to record, edit, and publish content directly on the platform without relying on third-party apps.

    In a recent development, A key addition is an upgraded media editor that lets creators produce polished vertical videos without leaving X. Recording features include the ability to capture video in segments and use green-screen effects, the company remarked.

    It has been revealed that the editor also offers a range of postproduction tools. Creators can convert horizontal videos to vertical format, automatically generate captions, trim footage, add text overlays, choose custom thumbnails, and adjust photos before publishing.

    Thanks to a recently announced update, users can now add up to 20 photos and videos to a single post, which audiences can swipe through horizontally. X claims the feature is intended for sharing event recaps, behind-the-scenes moments, and product launches.

    Availability of the upcoming features varies by region, X said.

    Recent findings suggest that earlier this month, the organization introduced a clipping feature that lets people take snippets from longer videos, add their own commentary, and post the clips without leaving X. Clips credit and link to the original video, plus the person who creates a clip and the original poster can earn from its views.

    Another feature, “React with Video,” launched earlier this year. Similar to TikTok’s “stitch” feature, this lets creators respond to posts with video commentary while displaying the original post in the background.

    It has been revealed that X has also introduced new earning opportunities and updates to its creator monetization programs in recent months. These include the “Video Kickstart Bonus,” an invitation-only pilot that rewards selected creators for publishing original vertical videos under three minutes long and without watermarks.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • FIFA told news agencies on Thursday that it had been targeted by a person or group seeking access to its data.
    • "FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to a limited set of personal and business information," a FIFA spokesperson told the Reuters news agency, issuing similar comments to other outlets.
    • Reuters cited a person "with direct knowledge of the matter" as saying that less than 0.1% of FIFA's total data had been compromised.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    FIFA told news agencies on Thursday that it had been targeted by a person or group seeking access to its data.

    "FIFA can confirm that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to a limited set of personal and business information," a FIFA spokesperson told the Reuters news agency, issuing similar comments to other outlets.

    Reuters cited a person "with direct knowledge of the matter" as saying that less than 0.1% of FIFA's total data had been compromised.

    This person also said that no files from the controversial, abandoned FIFA Forward Enterprise project that looked to sell a stake in the World Cup to private investors had been accessed.

    FIFA said that it was working closely with the relevant authorities, including law enforcement, in the aftermath of the event.

    It did not say when the attack took place, list the precise nature of the compromised data or specify how unauthorized access to FIFA data had been sought, amid reports of people having posed as FIFA officials rather than actually hacking the organization or otherwise compromising its cybersecurity systems.

    Recent findings suggest that "FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," the Zurich-based organization noted. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned.".

    Last week, a group calling itself the Handsome Boy Hacking Club posted a screenshot of what it mentioned were FIFA files. Three days later, it appeared to take credit for the cyberattack when responding to a post saying that more than 12 gigabytes of internal documents had been posted.

    FIFA did not explicitly state whether it was talking about the same supposed incident.

    The breach comes at a sensitive time for the organization. Still reeling from the scandal following this summer's World Cup of its now-aborted plans to sell off World Cup commercial rights shares, it's now trying to secure another term for its embattled president, Gianni Infantino.

    Infantino is the favorite for an election on March 18, when he is expected toface challenges from Kohzo Tashima of Japan and Philippe Diallo of France. But until the turbulence of the last six months, it seemed most likely he would simply stand unopposed and extend his 11-year tenure without a fight.

    Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Watch: Taylor on the 'overwhelming reaction' to Duran Duran's music.
    • Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.
    • Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: Taylor on the 'overwhelming reaction' to Duran Duran's music.

    Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65.

    Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film.

    Le Bon and his bandmates paid tribute, saying "he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music", while Sir Rod remembered his "dear pal" and Spandau Ballet's Kemp called him "a great player who set the tone for the 80s".

    Taylor's wife Tracey called him "the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day." He died after "a long and courageous battle with prostate cancer", Duran Duran stated in a statement on Wednesday.

    Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a Wild Boy on stage and off.

    He died "peacefully at home, surrounded by his family, on Monday 23rd November", a statement said.

    Paying tribute, his Duran Duran bandmates mentioned: "From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music.

    "His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.".

    They remarked their thoughts were with his wife, children and grandson.

    Le Bon said there was a "a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart".

    "Andy never took the easy musical route. His overdrive overdrove us into being the only funk/rock/punk band in the Upcoming Romantic movement, with songs that still survive, decades later.".

    Watch: Andy Taylor tells the BBC about his cancer diagnosis in 2023.

    Sir Rod, who wrote five songs with Taylor for the 1988 album Out of Order, recalled them making "some good music together" and having "some outrageous fun".

    Kemp noted Taylor "influenced many of us along the way with his sparse staccato style", adding: "He brought shameless rock to the mix.".

    In a band tribute, Spandau Ballet called him "a hugely talented musician and an important part of the British music scene".

    US guitarist Nile Rodgers, the co-founder of Chic, recalled "countless great days and nights" with his "dear friend".

    Belinda Carlisle mentioned she was "blessed" to have worked with Taylor, who played the guitar solo and was in the video for her song Mad About You.

    Former Led Zeppelin frontman Robert Plant called Taylor "a tough fighter", while Then Jerico's Mark Shaw remembered him as "one of the greatest musicians and songwriters I've ever heard and had the privilege to work with".

    Taylor (second left) married his wife Tracey at the Chateau Marmont hotel in Los Angeles in 1982.

    Taylor's wife Tracey, a hairstylist he met during the early days of Duran Duran, and whom he married in 1982, noted: "For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first for Taylor, adding: "Nothing made him happier than having us all together.".

    She said he faced the last few years "with so much courage and determination" and said they were "grateful" for the "kindness and support shown to him by fans throughout his illness", saying it brought him "immense comfort and strength".

    Andy Taylor's guitar riffs powered some of Duran Duran's best-known songs.

    The son of a fisherman, Taylor taught himself guitar, bass, and drums and began playing professionally at age 13.

    He played with several bands around the UK before answering a music paper advertisement for a "live-wire guitarist", which led to his audition for Duran Duran in Birmingham in April 1980.

    The group went on to achieve global fame through the New Romantic movement, which combined slick, melodic synth-pop with aspirational music videos and chiselled good looks.

    Taylor's guitar lines - full of glassy, powerful riffs - were often a highlight of their songs, from the choppy opening of Girls on Film to the sleazy scuzz of Hungry Like The Wolf.

    Duran Duran bridged the sounds of pop, funk, disco, punk and new wave with a sound that remains indelibly tied to the 1980s.

    Duran Duran were one of the biggest pop acts of the 1980s, and its five members became global hearththrobs.

    Their indelible hooks and airbrushed music videos found a natural home on the newly released MTV, giving their career a huge boost in the US.

    They became so popular in the US that the press labeled them the leaders of a "second British invasion" of the charts - alongside groups like Spandau Ballet, Human League and Eurythmics.

    During a hiatus in 1984, Andy and John Taylor enlisted Robert Palmer for their successful but short-lived side project the Power Station.

    The following year, the guitarist decided to quit Duran Duran after a miserable experience performing at Live Aid.

    "We'd reached rock bottom and we had absolutely nothing to say to each other," he wrote in his autobiography, Wild Boy.

    "We drove to the venue through streets packed with excited rock fans, but inside the bus the atmosphere was as if we were on a way to a funeral.".

    He went on to play on Palmer's Addicted To Love, and released a solo album, Thunder, in 1987.

    Taylor quit Duran Duran at the height of their fame in 1985, but rejoined the band several times in the 2000s and contributed to their most recent album, Danse Macabre.

    After a period writing and producing albums for other artists, he rejoined Duran Duran in 2000, lasting for just one album (2004's Astronaut) before parting ways again.

    In 2022, when the band were inducted to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Taylor was notably absent from the ceremony, despite public plans for a reunion.

    When the group took the stage, Le Bon read a letter from the guitarist, in which he revealed his diagnosis with stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer.

    Nonetheless, he contributed to the following year's Halloween-themed album Danse Macabre, marking his final collaboration with the band.

    The following BBC programmes will pay tribute to Taylor:.

    Duran Duran at the BBC, on BBC Four on Friday 27 November at 21:30 GMT.

    Sounds of the 80s, on Radio 2 on Saturday 28 November at at 18:00 GMT.

    Andy Taylor: Duran Duran's livewire guitarist who was a true Wild Boy.

    #207807. Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (982 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (982 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements.
    • In a recent development, after four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux.
    • Ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault.

    In a recent development, after four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious people had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it’s an installable package with automatic updating.

    Ladybird is most notable for what it isn’t: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google’s Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird’s rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. “The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork,” project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday’s announcement. “The browser around it is modest, but functional.”.

    Recent findings suggest that nearly the entire modern web currently runs on three browser engines. There’s WebKit (Safari), Gecko (Firefox), and the biggest of them all, Blink (Chromium). Those limited options mean that web developers often end up optimizing sites for Chromium specifically, since that’s where the majority of traffic is, and as a result, the whole web platform tends to follow suit toward whatever the dominant engine supports.

    Recent findings suggest that an independent implementation of web standards has value not just by providing additional competition in the market, but because it can’t help but reveal places where sites depend on Chromium behaviors rather than published specifications. The fact that Ladybird exists isn’t likely to shift the market tides any time soon, but every latest browser engine increases the number of implementations that standards can be tested against, which can surface Chromium-specific assumptions and push the ecosystem toward the spec.

    According to recent reports, the Ladybird project was borne out of Kling’s SerenityOS project, an attempt to develop a fresh independent OS from scratch, before splitting off as a separate project. Kling formed the Ladybird Browser Initiative, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit funded by sponsorships and donations. The project’s site highlights that there are no sponsored search engine deals supporting the project like many other popular browsers, and sponsoring entities have no say in the project roadmap.

    The Ladybird alpha is a rolling release channel that updates automatically, and the downloadable package is a huge step to getting the browser onto the PCs of everyday users. “Ladybird improves quickly, and until now you had to build it from source to see that,” Kling wrote. Though the browser began as C++, in keeping with the ethos of SerenityOS, the project has since started shifting toward Rust, starting with its JavaScript engine.

    While it’s exciting to have a newly introduced engine option for browsing, the project leader notes that this is still a very early release. The browser build contains a built-in tool for reporting any websites that fail to render or crash the browser. Kling writes, “We want security nerds to hack it! A new browser gets hacked, over and over, and that’s part of the process, so we make no promises about security today.”.

    Microsoft users are still out in the cold on this one for now. The project says that future support for Windows is planned, but it’s macOS and Linux only for now.

    I tested the Ladybird alpha version 2026.47.8 on my AceMagic W1 mini PC AMD Ryzen 7 8745HS with 16GB DDR5 and running Fedora Linux 44 with the new KDE Plasma 6.8.3, and the most surprising thing about the alpha build was how little it feels like alpha software.

    The browser seemed to handle most anything I threw at it without glitch. Day-to-day tabbed browsing mechanics felt snappy and normal. A 50MB test video file downloaded swiftly and smoothly. With a dozen tabs open, switching between them was instant, and the browser felt responsive throughout. Options menus were surprisingly fleshed out for a build this young.

    Recent findings suggest that google Maps loaded instantly, located me, and handled everything I threw at it: adding and removing layers, zooming out from the Midwest, and dropping into Street View in Alberta, Canada in around three seconds. Everything rendered fast enough that my mini PC’s fan spun up noticeably. GitHub’s site, including repository navigation, worked without a hitch. So did YouTube and the news sites I tried.

    I could stall the browser, but it took some effort. With about 10 tabs open, I was streaming a 4K test video file from my personal Jellyfin server. Everything worked fine at first, but after skipping around in the file over and over again, the browser eventually got stuck. Mind you, this is an alpha build that I was trying to trip up, not a representation of something inherently broken.

    After spending an evening with Ladybird, I can say that while it won’t be replacing Firefox for me anytime soon, I was genuinely impressed that a scratch-made engine could perform this well in such an early state. Most latest browser projects are forks of something that already exists. Ladybird is the rare exception, an engine written from nothing, and the alpha runs well enough that if you have a Mac or Linux PC handy, it’s worth downloading a build and poking around yourself. Just remember Kling’s warning: This is nowhere near trustworthy enough to make your daily driver, yet.

    Industry observers note that what the alpha demonstrates is that a small team of independent developers, funded by donations, has built a browser engine from scratch that handles real web browsing without a fuss. That it works this well this soon, using no existing engine code, is an achievement. I thought I was a Firefox loyalist, but I’ll be keeping an eye on where this one goes.

    Character.AI’s initiative to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • What happens to your private conversations when an AI tech giant goes bankrupt?
    • Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of people.
    • Sources indicate that the attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    What happens to your private conversations when an AI tech giant goes bankrupt? If it’s Character.ai, apparently, the plan is to auction them off to the highest bidder.

    Now, a coalition of 42 state attorneys general is intervening in Character.ai’s bankruptcy proceedings in an effort to stop the chatbot maker from selling off sensitive user data, which includes the private conversations of millions of people.

    Sources indicate that the attorneys general involved in the matter have put out individual press releases, claiming that Character.ai’s dataset includes chat histories from more than 21 million U.S. accounts, more than 2.1 million of which belong to minors. In addition, the sale would involve other personal data, like IP addresses, the statements stated.

    Only one anonymous bidder for the chat data has been disclosed so far: Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC (Smirks), which was set up as a Delaware company on November 13, 2026. The following day, Character.ai picked it as the base bid for the auction, scheduled for December 1, California Attorney General Rob Bonta noted. It is unclear what the buyer’s aims are for the chats.

    In addition, some states, including California, Colorado, New York, and Connecticut, have enacted chatbot safety legislation that will go into effect on January 1, 2027, which could trigger further violations if the sale goes through.

    “Character.AI promised consumers that their data would not be sold. This kind of behavior is illegal under federal and California law and bankruptcy should not be used to sidestep these consumer protections,” Bonta said in a statement.

    Connecticut Attorney General William Tong also criticized Character.ai’s business model.

    “Their chatbots drove vulnerable youth down a rabbit hole of emotionally volatile and sexually inappropriate chats,” Tong noted. “Their reckless misconduct and broken business model drove their firm into the ground. Now they want to abuse the bankruptcy process to do exactly what they said they wouldn’t do — auction off those private chat records and personal details to a shady buyer.”.

    Tong added: “We objected to the Disney sale, and we’re calling on the bankruptcy court to reject this sale too as yet another guise to eviscerate legal liability and consumer protection.”.

    The opposition to the Disney sale was led by a similar but not identical coalition of state AGs. They fought against a proposed $20 million licensing deal that would give Disney access to Character.ai’s intellectual property, but not to customers’ chats. The deal has not yet received final court approval. (Disney also agreed to hire most of Character.ai’s remaining staff.).

    Recent findings suggest that character.ai suffered after its co-founders, Noam Shazeer and Daniel De Freitas, returned to Google, when the tech giant signed a non-exclusive license to use the AI startup’s tech. The firm also faced lawsuits related to child safety — one involved the suicide of a 14-year-old Florida boy whose mother claimed he had become obsessed with a chatbot on the platform.

    California AG Bonta is joined in the effort to oppose the sale of Character.ai user data by attorneys general from Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Delaware, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Nevada, Newly introduced Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, Vermont, Washington, Wisconsin, and West Virginia.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Laura Freigang is set to miss next year's women's World Cup in Brazil after being suspended for missing doping tests, the German Football Association (DFB) said in a statement on Thursday.

    In a recent development, freigang, who has played 45 matches for Germany and scored 17 goals, will be suspended until October 7, 2027 after reaching a settlement with the DFB, the World Anti-Doping Agency and Germany's National Anti-Doping Agency. The suspension is for the next 16 months as it began retroactively on June 8, 2026, when she was notified by the DFB, and prohibits Freigang from playing for club or country.

    "It's vital to me to emphasize once again that I was never suspected of doping," Freigang noted in a statement on Instagram.

    "My agreement to a settlement does not mean that I share all the assessments of my case. The past few months have been extremely difficult for me. Another legal process would have entailed significant financial, mental, and emotional strain. This is why I decided to take this path, in the hope of finding some peace, clarity and perspective for myself," she added.

    "It was never my intention to let it get this far. Sports have defined my life since I was little. It breaks my heart that, for now, I won't be able to step onto the field, help my team, or live the daily life that I love so much.".

    Recent findings suggest that this brings to a close a case that has been ongoing for months. The 28-year-old had been accused of not being where she said she would be for a doping control on three occasions between March 2025 and February 2026.

    In June, Freigang explained missing the tests "were not deliberately avoided appointments but inconsistencies or misunderstandings in the comprehensive details that have to be updated daily and which we as national team players have to enhancement in the system on a daily and hourly basis.".

    The ban ends her World Cup hopes, something the DFB has also acknowledged.

    "We are simply so sorry for Laura on a personal level because of this situation. The past few weeks have been very stressful for her," said DFB Sporting Director Nia Künzer. "We hold her in high regard both as a player and as a person, and — as we have done in recent weeks — we will continue to stay in touch with her and support her as best we can.".

    Recent findings suggest that the situation also puts her future at her club, Eintracht Frankfurt, into question. Freigang's contract runs until June next year.

    "The agreement that has now been reached provides clarity and planning certainty through a process that is unique to Eintracht Frankfurt — for us as a club, but above all for Laura," stated Katharina Kiel, Frankfurt's director of women's football.

    The club and Freigang, who has played 180 Bundesliga games in her career, are now set to enter talks to determine the shape of her contract moving forward.

    Upcoming York state bans AI chatbot toys for kids

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Companies violating the five year ban will face a $15,000 per day fine.
    • It has been revealed that fresh York governor Kathy Hochul has signed into law a five-year ban on the sale of AI chatbot toys, including dolls and robots that use the internet to converse with children.
    • "Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," Hochul said in a statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Companies violating the five year ban will face a $15,000 per day fine.

    It has been revealed that fresh York governor Kathy Hochul has signed into law a five-year ban on the sale of AI chatbot toys, including dolls and robots that use the internet to converse with children. The new law comes with some teeth, including steep daily fines for each violation enforced by the state's attorney general.

    "Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk," Hochul said in a statement. Calling herself Latest York's first "mom governor," Hochul said the new measure was "deeply personal.".

    According to recent reports, the governor's press release cited the US Public Interest Research Group Education Fund (PIRG), that tested chatbot toys marketed to children aged three to 12. Some of the toys talked about sexually explicit subjects and provided advice that could create a fire hazard in homes. The toys had few or zero parental controls and the longer the conversation, the more safety limits weakened. Some toys could even record a child's voice or scan their face.

    "AI chatbots in children's toys are exposing young people to inappropriate content and putting their mental health at risk," said Upcoming York attorney general Letitia James.

    Recent findings suggest that violators face civil penalties up to $15,000 per day for each violation, according to the governor's office. James added that her branch would "not hesitate to enforce this law and other measures to stop AI systems from doing harm. We won't allow our children's health to become the collateral damage of significant tech.".

    Recent findings suggest that hochul and Latest York State legislators recently enacted another law called "AI Chatbot Restrictions for Minors," prohibiting unsafe chatbot features for children under 18, with civil penalties of up to $25,000 per infraction. Hochul also signed an executive order this summer, issuing a one-year ban data centers using 50MW or more.

    Anti-AI measures were a politically popular during US midterm elections, as Americans voted to restrict the country's data center boom. Data centers were the subject of 45 ballot measures in 10 states and 39 measures were passed to restrict the facilities in some form.

    According to recent reports, in a statement, Amazon stated the products it sells must follow US laws. "We require all products sold by third-party sellers in our store to comply with applicable laws and regulations," Amazon told NBC News. "Amazon is committed to the safety of children and families. We support efforts across the industry and government to put appropriate guardrails in place as this technology develops." However, the retail giant sells some 12 million different toys in the US (as of 2023), so complying with the NY AI chatbot law could be a tall order.

    Tech Report: Myanmar refuses to comply with parts of ICJ genocide ruling

    📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing has led the country since he seized power in a 2021 military coup.
    • Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.
    • The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Myanmar's president Min Aung Hlaing has led the country since he seized power in a 2021 military coup.

    Myanmar will not comply with "inappropriate" parts of the genocide ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ), its leader Min Aung Hlaing has said in his first public comments since the court decision.

    The ICJ's landmark ruling last week found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority in a 2017 military crackdown that killed thousands and forced more than 700,000 to flee.

    According to recent reports, myanmar denied committing genocide, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups. It is the first state to have been found in violation of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

    Min Aung Hlaing noted "the term 'genocide' had seriously affected the country's reputation", state media report.

    "Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," the country's coup leader-turned-president said at a meeting on Wednesday, according to state media.

    The statement did not specify which parts of the ruling the country objects to.

    The genocide case, brought by The Gambia in 2019, centred around so-called "clearance operations" initiated in 2017 in Rakhine State, where many of the Rohingya Muslim minority resided.

    The ICJ determined that about 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed during the operation, while more than 700,000 are thought to have fled to Bangladesh by foot or by sea. The court found that approximately 815,000 had been targeted in some way.

    The verdict was reached by a majority of nine votes to six among a panel of judges from around the world.

    The ICJ also found in favour by majority that Myanmar had violated several other parts of the 1948 Genocide Convention.

    The ruling is final and cannot be appealed.

    The ICJ ordered Myanmar to pay proportionate reparations, but said an exact figure should be determined at a later date.

    The court also ordered Myanmar to stop ongoing violations and immediately investigate those suspected of breaking the Convention.

    It has been revealed that but the ICJ does not have the power to enforce these demands. Instead it has to rely on the UN Security Council and political pressure to make its rulings stick.

    While the ruling was largely symbolic, it was welcomed by Rohingya communities and human rights groups who have long called attention to the suffering faced by the Rohingya.

    More than a dozen countries have acknowledged the ICJ ruling, and the UK has unveiled sanctions on several senior Myanmar military leaders.

    Myanmar has been devastated by civil war since Min Aung Hlaing led a military coup to oust civilian leader Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. The move turned Myanmar into an international pariah, and its military regime has faced sweeping international sanctions.

    Since then, Min Aung Hlaing has been trying to reintegrate Myanmar into the international community, but it remains largely shut out of key diplomatic arenas.

    #207795. The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.
    • If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.
    • “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers.

    If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold.

    “The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. “This action opens a bold latest frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth.”.

    The decision, confirmed a day before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States, represents a major regulatory victory for SpaceX and its founder, Elon Musk, who has allied himself with the Trump administration.

    This announcement clears a major hurdle to deploying data centers in space, although it does not establish that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable. Nevertheless, the FCC authorization appears designed to give the manufacturer wide latitude as it works through these remaining issues.

    For example, SpaceX has seven years to deploy a single operational Starmind satellite under the order. SpaceX has until November 2035 to deploy 100,000 operational satellites, and November 2040 for the full constellation. SpaceX, therefore, has a 14-year regulatory runway to deploy the most ambitious industrial project ever approved for spaceflight.

    Sources indicate that the authorization includes some conditional aspects. SpaceX has proposed operating in six orbits, ranging from 550 km to about 1,000 km. The organization sought a waiver from FCC rules to allow satellites above 600 km to be disposed of into “Earth disposal orbits or heliocentric orbits.” That is, instead of burning them up in Earth’s atmosphere, SpaceX wants the flexibility to move retired satellites into other orbits around Earth, or potentially into orbit around the Sun.

    The FCC did not grant this waiver request “because SpaceX has not provided sufficient information for the Commission to determine whether its alternative disposal methods are compliant with the Commission’s requirements.” The tech giant will need to obtain a waiver before deploying any Starmind satellites that are not intended to be disposed of via atmospheric reentry.

    Recent findings suggest that however, in other ways the FCC appears to have been incredibly lenient with SpaceX. This is particularly the case with environmental concerns raised by numerous parties that commented on SpaceX’s application to the FCC.

    Half a dozen organizations, such as the Secure World Foundation and American Astronomical Society, raised concerns about deploying so many satellites into orbit, citing collision risks, orbital debris, atmospheric pollution from so many satellite reentries, impacts on astronomical observations, and more. The FCC also received approximately 1,500 public comments concerning SpaceX’s application.

    Some of these environmental issues, the FCC noted, lay beyond the scope of its review. For example, on concerns about the environmental implications of thousands or potentially tens of thousands of rocket debuts, the FCC said, “Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview.”.

    According to recent reports, the FCC also rejected calls for further environmental scrutiny of pollution from satellite reentries, including concerns about aluminum oxides and their potential effects on the ozone layer. “Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record,” the FCC authorization states.

    In a recent development, as part of its decision, the FCC cited a significant policy change adopted in October, when the agency concluded that space-based activities generally fall outside its obligations under the National Environmental Policy Act. The FCC reasoned that as these activities occur beyond US territory, they don’t constitute federal actions requiring environmental review. As a result, the agency declined to conduct a comprehensive environmental assessment of SpaceX’s Starmind constellation.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The study will evaluate the efficacity and safety of the company’s LINK device.

    Elon Musk's Neuralink has received FDA permission to launch the first "pivotal" trial for its implantable LINK brain-computer interface, the manufacturer announced. The study represents a more advanced step in the company's efforts to develop a brain implant that allows people with paralysis to control devices using their brain alone. It will be open to a limited number of patients with ALS (amyotrophic lateral sclerosis), a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that damages nerve cells controlling voluntary muscle movement.

    According to recent reports, "We've received FDA approval to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface in the US," Neuralink confirmed on X. "This builds off of our work with 30+ participants with Neuralink to date.".

    It has been revealed that neuralink hit a milestone last year when the company revealed that its first participant with ALS named Bradford Smith was able to communicate using brain signals alone. "Neuralink has given me freedom, hope, and faster communication. ... It has improved my life so much. I'm so happy to be involved in something big that will help many people," Smith stated at the time.

    Sources indicate that we've received FDA approval to launch LINK, the first pivotal trial for an implantable brain-computer interface in the US. This builds off of our work with 30+ participants with Neuralink to date.

    According to recent reports, those with ALS may be eligible. To learn more:https://t.co/dWhb5N4GdR pic.twitter.com/Vor7iXXCBA.

    — Neuralink (@neuralink) November 25, 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that the FDA authorization was granted on an experimental basis, but it's a key step forward for Neuralink's LINK brain-implant system. The study will evaluate the ability of patients to control digital devices through thought, "with a focus on functional outcomes that improve independence in daily life," Neuralink wrote. It will also assess the system's long-term safety and reliability.

    WIth Neuralink's latest system, the manufacturer's N1 implant is surgically placed in the skull, then the company uses its R1 robot to insert flexible electrodes into the brain. Neural activity from the brain associated with movement is then interpreted by software, which translates signals into commands for controlling computers or digital devices. The technology is designed to help patients communicate with the outside world, with the eventual goal to let them operate devices without keyboards or other physical controls.

    Industry observers note that neuralink mentioned patients with ALS may be eligible for the LINK trial, but it didn't specify other requirements or the number of participants. It now has approval recruit participants, then conduct the study under an approved clinical protocol. If the technology proves to be safe, the trial may allow Neuralink to apply for more advanced trials and eventually release LINK onto the market.

    DOJ accuses former cyber executive of defrauding ransomware victims by secretly paying hackers

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the company could get their encrypted files back.
    • It has been revealed that according to federal prosecutors, Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware.
    • But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The U.S. Department of Justice has indicted a former executive of a ransomware recovery firm after he allegedly defrauded victims of cyberattacks by claiming the company could get their encrypted files back.

    It has been revealed that according to federal prosecutors, Juan Ricardo Palacio Escobar, 52, was the chief technology officer at RansomwareHelp, which purported to offer data recovery services to victims of ransomware. The company’s website, which currently reads as “under maintenance,” claimed it could decrypt hacked data by using its proprietary technology, according to an archived copy of the site from earlier this year. RansomwareHelp touted a success rate of “over 99%.”.

    But the company allegedly had no technical ability to unscramble data and instead “negotiated with and paid a ransom to the ransomware actors to decrypt the victim data,” while charging the ransomware victim more and keeping the difference,” per the Justice Department’s statement.

    Palacio Escobar then allegedly used the funds to buy several properties in Florida.

    The DOJ stated the FBI carried out an undercover operation in June, in part posing as a company that claimed it had been hit by ransomware. The company claimed to the undercover agents that it never negotiated with hackers or paid a ransom. But then Palacio Escobar paid the apparent hackers some $6,000 in cryptocurrency, without the knowledge that FBI agents were also posing as the ransomware hackers.

    404 Media first reported the indictment last week against Palacio Escobar. He faces three charges of wire fraud, and could receive 20 years in prison on each count.

    Palacio Escobar is the latest, albeit rare, example of cybersecurity professionals going rogue. Earlier this year, two ransomware negotiators working for cybersecurity companies were jailed on hacking and extortion charges, after being caught moonlighting with the ransomware gangs that they were ostensibly investigating. A third ransomware negotiator was also convicted of helping hackers deploy ransomware against several companies.

    Last month, independent cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs reported that FBI agents arrested a Canadian cybersecurity executive in Philadelphia on allegations that he was involved with the theft of FBI personnel records by the hacking and extortion gang ShinyHunters. The hacking group told TechCrunch that they took credit for the theft of FBI data in September, which they stated they would not publicly release, a departure from its earlier extortion-based cyberattacks.

    The federal charges against the Canadian cybersecurity executive relate to conspiracy to commit extortion, though much of the court docket — and his alleged links to the hacking group — remains under seal.
